chunks: The Shaykh, may Allah Most High support him, informed me from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from his father, from al-Husayn ibn al-Hasan ibn Aban, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from al-Nadr, from Ibn Sinan, who said:

I heard Aba 'Abdillah عليه السلام saying: "If a man does not find any means of purification and he is in janabah, then let him wipe from the earth and perform salat (prayer). Then when he finds water, let him perform ghusl (ritual bath), and the salat (prayer) that he performed has sufficed him."

key_terms.أَجْزَأَتْهُ: it has sufficed him; it counts as valid and adequate
key_terms.الْأَرْضِ: the earth, used as the medium for tayammum
key_terms.جُنُبًا: being in a state of janabah requiring ghusl
key_terms.فَلْيَغْتَسِلْ: let him perform ghusl when water is found
key_terms.فَلْيَمْسَحْ: let him wipe, referring here to tayammum

ai.seo_question: What should a junub person do if no water is available for purification before salat (prayer)?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling for a person in janabah who cannot find water. He should perform tayammum using the earth and offer salat (prayer), and when water becomes available, he should perform ghusl, while the earlier prayer remains valid and sufficient.
